subject: Hydra trial: capacity buffer & TPS/latency fit
content:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@hydrainc.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hydra trial — tokens/sec headroom ask

Alex —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As mentioned, we're kicking off a 6-week trial to validate UX latency and cost for our assistant flows. High level: typical session generates ~250–350 output tokens, peak concurrent active sessions expected ~60 during US business hours, and we want to validate a p95 latency target of <=500ms for the generation step.

Can you send a short runbook-style sizing recommendation (tokens/sec target, GPUs to reserve, and a brief fallback strategy) so we can align procurement? We need something we can present to our infra team and procurement this week.

Thanks — Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Engineering, Hydra Inc.

---

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@hydrainc.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hydra trial — tokens/sec headroom ask

Liam —

Appreciate the details. Attached is a concise proposal and a short simulation workbook (hydra-multipass-sim.xlsx) that walks through two scenarios: 1) conservative (40% headroom) and 2) aggressive trial (20% headroom). Below is the TL;DR sizing and assumptions; Evelyn and Marcus are looped for the nitty-gritty.

Assumptions (from Hydra):
- avg generated tokens/session: 300 (input+gen ~ 350)
- peak concurrent active sessions: 60
- trial p95 target for generation step: <= 500ms
- model baseline: rwd-xl-70b (float16, quantized kernels)

Quick math (peak):
- tokens/sec needed at peak = concurrent_sessions * avg_tokens_per_session / avg_request_duration_seconds
- If we budget generation to complete in 0.45s (to hit p95 <= 500ms including network overhead), tokens/sec = 60 * 300 / 0.45 ≈ 40,000 tokens/sec

That's the gross tokens/sec we need to sustain at peak. I'm deliberately sizing for generation-only work (we'll handle prompt preprocessing outside of the GPU slab).

Initial recommendation (conservative):
- Reserved pool: 4 x H100-80GB equivalent GPUs (Redwood Dedicated slab)
- Measured sustained throughput per H100 for rwd-xl-70b with our batching & KV-cache = ~9,000 tokens/sec (observed in similar customers with similar prompt mix)
- Aggregate sustained capacity = 4 * 9,000 = 36,000 tokens/sec
- Headroom = ~10% short of the gross 40k estimate; recommend burst + shared capacity to cover instantaneous peaks or raise slab to 5 GPUs for 25% headroom.

Fallbacks & runbook notes:
- Canary fallback model: rwd-13b (quantized) — will reduce p95 but keep service usable under sustained overload.
- Auto-fallback policy: route to 13B when slab CPU/GPU queue latency > 200ms for > 30s.
- Caching: enable prefix KV-cache for repeated prompts to reduce tokens generated for short assistant edits (can cut effective TPS by up to 18% on our estimations).

Evelyn / Marcus — can you validate the per-GPU throughput number and confirm a recommended monthly slab commit and burst plan we should propose to procurement?

Thanks,
Alex

---

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hydra trial — tokens/sec headroom ask

Alex — quick validation and a tighter breakdown below. I ran a short sim using Hydra's numbers (attached workbook). Key pieces: model, sequence distribution, and p95 latency target drive buffer math.

Verified assumptions:
- Model: rwd-xl-70b, FP16 with kernel-level 4-bit QAT paths in production -> observed per-H100 sustained tokens/sec (steady-state, 95th percentile latency budgeted) = 8,800–9,300 t/s depending on batch mix. I'll use 9,000 t/s as a conservative median.
- Typical generation distribution: 40% short (<64 tokens), 45% medium (64–320), 15% long (>320). That pushes effective average tokens/session to 295 in sim.

Detailed sizing (calculation):
- Peak gross tokens/sec requirement = 60 concurrent * 295 tokens / 0.45s = 39,333 t/s ≈ 39.4k t/s.
- GPUs needed (no headroom) = ceil(39,333 / 9,000) = 5 GPUs -> aggregate 45k t/s
- If we accept 20% operational headroom during trial (recommended for noisy traffic and performance variance): required = ceil(39,333 * 1.20 / 9,000) = ceil(47,200 / 9,000) = 6 GPUs -> 54k t/s
- If we accept 10% headroom (balanced): 5 GPUs (45k t/s) gives ~14% headroom vs gross; close but acceptable for a short trial with burst cover.

Recommendation summary for procurement doc:
- Trial minimum: 5 x H100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated) — this meets gross need and gives modest headroom.
- Conservative trial (recommended): 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs — targets 20% headroom and smoother p95 compliance.
- Burst plan: allow access to 2 additional shared GPUs during US business-hour peaks (auto-burst) to absorb microspikes without immediate fallback to smaller models.

Operational notes:
- Latency SLO mapping: with 6 GPUs our p95 sim for generation step falls to ~420ms (including batching inefficiencies and KV-cache misses). With 5 GPUs p95 hovers ~480–520ms depending on request mix.
- Cost-impact note: each additional H100-equivalent adds ~18–22% to monthly committed spend for this slab; simulations attached show cost per 1k requests at both 5 and 6 GPU options.

I'll attach the simulation and a short one-pager for procurement (redwood-proposal-hydra.pdf). Marcus — can you add a short paragraph for the ops runbook (alerts/thresholds + escalation path)?

Evelyn

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@hydrainc.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hydra trial — capacity buffer & TPS/latency fit

Liam / team — adding a short ops blurb you can paste into your runbook.

Ops runbook (excerpt):
- Metrics to monitor: per-GPU queue depth, per-request generation time, cluster tokens/sec, p95 generation latency, KV-cache hit rate.
- Alerts (suggested):
  - WARN: queue depth > 6 for > 60s on any GPU -> notify on-call and scale burst pool.
  - SEV: queue depth > 12 for > 30s or p95 generation latency > 650ms for 2 consecutive 2-min windows -> trigger auto-fallback to rwd-13b and page SRE.
- Escalation: procurement & account exec are notified for sustained >15% breach in predicted capacity for >24h.
- Post-trial ops item: run an A/B split during week 3 to measure end-user perceived latency difference between 70B and 13B fallback for a representative cohort.

I'll include these as a short section in the attached PDF.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@hydrainc.com>, procurement@hydrainc.com
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 12:14:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposal: Hydra trial commitment options & next steps

Liam —

Thanks — attached are the two pickable options for trial procurement:
1) 5 x H100-equivalent GPUs (trial-min): meets gross tokens/sec and is lower cost; expect p95 generation ~480–520ms depending on mix.
2) 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs (recommended): ~20% headroom, p95 generation ~420ms in our sim.

We recommend option (2) for a smoother test and cleaner SLA validation. For both options we propose an auto-burst policy that can add up to 2 shared GPUs during transient peaks (billing: metered per-minute). We can lock a short 6-week reserved commitment for the trial to keep costs predictable; proposal highlights are in the attached PDF.

Can we confirm the preferred option by end-of-day Friday so procurement has time to route the contract? I'm available Thurs/Fri for a 30-minute walk-through with your infra and procurement team — propose Thu 10am PT.

Documents attached:
- redwood-proposal-hydra.pdf (proposal + pricing for options 1 & 2)
- hydra-multipass-sim.xlsx (workbook with the sim and sensitivity knobs)

Next steps:
- Hydra confirms option 1 or 2 (+ whether they want commit pricing for the 6-week trial)
- We provision a Dedicated slab and share access to Canary env for initial traffic gating
- Week 1: sanity traffic, Week 2–5: ramp and A/B, Week 6: review & decide commit/expand

Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood proposal: Hydra trial commitment options & next steps

Appreciate the fast turnaround — this is great and very helpful. Procurement is leaning to option 2 (6 GPUs) so we'll plan to route the 6-week commit. Please go ahead and prepare the short-form order for signature (DocuSign).

We'd like Thu 10am PT for the walk-through. I'll send a calendar invite and loop our infra lead (cc'd on the invite).

— Liam
